7                    UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT                            
8                  SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA                           
9                                                                            
10  VIKING THERAPEUTICS, INC.,           Case No.:  3:22-cv-02062-H-VET       

11                             Plaintiff,                                     
                                        ORDER GRANTING, IN PART, AND         
12  v.                                   DENYING, IN PART, RIMON, P.C.’S      
                                        MOTION TO WITHDRAW AS                
13  ASCLETIS BIOSCIENCE CO., LTD.;                                            
                                        COUNSEL                              
   GANNEX PHARMA CO., LTD.;                                                  
14                                                                            
   ASCLETIS PHARMACEUTICALS CO.,                                             
                                        [Doc. No. 36.]                       
15  LTD.; ASCLETIS PHARMA INC.; and                                           
   JINZI JASON WU,                                                           
16                                                                            
                           Defendants.                                       
17                                                                            
18       On April 3, 2023, the Court stayed the present action pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1659(a) 
19  pending the final decision in ITC Investigation No. 337-TA-1352.  (Doc. No. 31.)  On 
20  February 5, 2024, Michael F. Heafey and Matthew H. Poppe of Rimon, P.C. (“Rimon”), 
21  counsel currently representing Defendants Ascletis Bioscience Co., Ltd., Gannex Pharma 
22  Co., Ltd., Ascletis Pharmaceuticals Co. Ltd., Ascletis Pharma Inc., and Jinzi Jason Wu 
23  (collectively, “Defendants”), filed a motion to withdraw as counsel in this action for 
24  Defendants.  (Doc. No. 36.)  On February 23, 2024, Plaintiff Viking Therapeutics, Inc. 
25  (“Plaintiff”) filed a response in opposition to Rimon’s motion to withdraw as counsel.  
26  (Doc.  No. 37.)    On  March  4,  2024,  Rimon  filed  a  reply.    (Doc.  No. 38.)    On 
27  March 12, 2024, the Court, pursuant to its discretion under Local Rule 7.1(d)(1), submitted 
28  the motion on the parties’ papers.  (Doc. No. 40.)  The Court further directed Rimon to 
1  provide contact information for Defendant Wu.  (Id.)  On March 19, 2024, Rimon filed 
2  supplemental briefing regarding Defendant Wu’s contact information.  (Doc. No. 41.)  On 
3  March 20, 2024, Plaintiff filed a response to Rimon’s supplemental briefing.  (Doc. 
4  No. 42.)  On March 21, 2024, Rimon filed additional supplemental briefing regarding 
5  Defendant Wu’s contact information.  (Doc. No. 44.)                       
6       Rimon seeks to withdraw because “Defendants have refused to pay a large amount 
7  of  money  to  Rimon  for  representing  Defendants  in  both  this  case  and  in  a  parallel 
8  proceeding pending in the U.S. International Trade Commission,” and has attached a 
9  declaration attesting to the same and to the non-prejudicial nature of the motion.  (Doc. 
10  No. 36 at 4; Doc. No. 36-1, Declaration of Juan Zuniga.)                  
11       Parties generally may plead and conduct their own cases personally. 28 U.S.C. 
12  § 1654.  However, “[o]nly natural persons representing their individual interests in propria 
13  persona may appear in court without representation by an attorney.”  Civ. L.R. 83.3(j).  
14  “All other parties, including corporations, partnerships and other legal entities, may appear 
15  in court only through an attorney permitted to practice pursuant to Civil Local Rule 83.3.”  
16  Id.; see also Rowland v. Cal. Men’s Colony, 506 U.S. 194, 201–02 (1993) (“It has been 
17  the law for the better part of two centuries . . . that a corporation may appear in the federal 
18  courts only through licensed counsel . . . . [T]hat rule applies equally to all artificial 
19  entities.”); United States v. High Country Broadcasting Co., Inc., 3 F.3d 1244, 1245 (9th 
20  Cir. 1993) (affirming district court’s entry of default judgment against the corporation 
21  when the corporation failed to retain counsel for the duration of the litigation).  
22       Here,  Rimon  seeks  to  withdraw  as  counsel  of  record  for  Defendant  Wu,  an 
23  individual,  and  corporate  Defendants  Ascletis  Bioscience,  Gannex  Pharma,  Ascletis 
24  Pharmaceuticals, and Ascletis Pharma.  Should Rimon be permitted to withdraw as counsel 
25  of  record  for  all  Defendants,  Ascletis  Bioscience,  Gannex  Pharma,  Ascletis 
26  Pharmaceuticals, and Ascletis Pharma would be without counsel in this action.  No counsel 
27  has appeared on behalf of Ascletis Bioscience, Gannex Pharma, Ascletis Pharmaceuticals, 
28  and Ascletis Pharma.  Consequently, permitting this withdrawal would leave Ascletis 
1  || Bioscience, Gannex Pharma, Ascletis Pharmaceuticals,  and Ascletis Pharma, “artificial” 
2          entities, proceeding without counsel in direct contravention to this District’s  Civil 
3    Local Rules.  See Civ. L.R. 83.34); Rowland, 506 U.S. at 201-02. 
4         In  light of the  foregoing,  the  Court  grants,  in part,  and  denies,  in part,  Rimon’s 
5   ||motion  to  withdraw  as  counsel  without  prejudice.   (Doc.  No.  36.)   The  Court  grants 
6   ||Rimon’s motion to withdraw as to Defendant Jinzi  Jason Wu.  The Clerk of the Court is 
7   ||instructed  to  update  Defendant  Wu’s  contact  information  as  follows: (1)  Mailing 
8 || Address: 6  Fuchun  Road,  Shangcheng  District,  Hanghzhou,  Zhejiang,  China,  310008; 
9   ||and (2) Telephone Number: +86 15088769922. 
10         The Court denies without prejudice Rimon’s motion to withdraw as to Defendants 
11 || Ascletis Bioscience, Gannex Pharma, Ascletis Pharmaceuticals, and Ascletis Pharma.  The 
12   ||Court temporarily lifts  the  stay to  allow Ascletis  Bioscience,  Gannex Pharma,  Ascletis 
13   ||Pharmaceuticals,  and Ascletis Pharma thirty (30) days to obtain substitute counsel and 
14   ||have  counsel  file  a notice  of appearance.   Should  such  Defendants  fail  to  obtain new 
15   |}counsel  within the  next thirty  days,  Rimon may  file  a renewed  motion no  earlier than 
16 || May 9, 2024, to withdraw as counsel of record.  If a renewed motion is filed, it should 
17 || describe the ongoing efforts to seek new counsel in addition to the ongoing relationship 
18 || with Ascletis Bioscience, Gannex Pharma, Ascletis Pharmaceuticals, and Ascletis Pharma. 
19   ||In  the  event  that  Ascletis  Bioscience,  Gannex  Pharma,  Ascletis  Pharmaceuticals,  and 
20 || Ascletis Pharma retain new counsel within the next thirty days, Rimon may immediately 
21   ||seek leave to withdraw as  counsel.  Upon resolution of Rimon’s  efforts to withdraw as 
22    counsel, the Court will reimpose the stay pending the final decision in ITC Investigation 
23   ||No. 337-TA-1352. 
24         IT IS SO ORDERED. 
25  || DATED: April 8, 2024                         | ul       |.    | | 
26                                             MARILYN   #. HUFF,  Distri      ge 
27                                             UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT 
28
